summary.name: Oil Painting / Gouache. Supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection.
summary.visualIdentity: Painterly, material-driven look built on one primary medium: oil with varied paint thickness and visible brushwork, or gouache with matte, opaque color masses. Explicitly, the medium must be chosen once, and lighting and palette must stay coherent. Lighting direction and subject matter are unspecified.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly supported: painted intros and landscape stories built from layered paint planes, and single gouache poster layouts with one subtle loop for event or social promos. Inferred: art-led explainers where a painted look carries the narrative. Interactive HTML can use layered images with a static fallback.
summary.limitations: Generic material filters are not allowed; repainting must come from prepared paint layers and coverage masks. Oil impasto and matte gouache must not be mixed on the same object. Avoid excess parallax, busy loops, glossy effects, and fake brush jitter. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production, and stateful simulations must be cached. Dimensions, scenes, and aspect ratios are unspecified optional examples.
summary.palette: The palette is an authored example, not a supplied or canonical style palette. Tokens: background #F1E6CF (dominant field), foreground #3E4C48 (primary text), accent_1 #9B604C, accent_2 #A89656, accent_3 #63818A (decorative, subordinate). Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 7.272:1, meeting the 4.5:1 normal-text target. Accent-based text pairings (accent_1 with background at 4.066, accent_2 with foreground at 3.071, accent_3 with background at 3.367) fail and are decorative only. Task or approved colors override these, and two-color checks do not verify text over textures or video.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicitly, motion is painterly: repainting, brush reveals, and layered scenery, with no requirement that oil and gouache share one behavior. Optional motion references are motion-012 (chapter handoff) and motion-015 (story steps); each applies only if the scene's action supports it, and choosing neither is valid. Video schedules states on composition time. Interactive HTML maps scroll progress and needs static or reduced-motion states. Cadence and easing are unspecified.
summary.audio: Not specified by the source. Inferred suggestions: restrained audio that serves the topic, such as music, voiceover, ambience, sound accents, or silence. No mandatory layer, genre, tempo, or voice is assigned. Explicit user audio requirements take priority. Final checks should confirm speech intelligibility, balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization.
summary.assetRequirements: Prepared layered painting assets are required: alpha-channel layers or numbered frame sequences with consistent dimensions, clear naming, and a layer manifest. Assets must be inspected before composition. Medium-specific paint layers and coverage masks are needed for local repainting. Pillow in Python can crop, resize, composite, and create masks. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Missing assets are unspecified and must be stated. Krita Drawn Frame Sequences is an alternative route.
summary.combinations: style-101 (layered paint planes for scene depth in painted intros or landscapes): choose oil or gouache, never both; use only primary pigment tokens; keep lighting shared; avoid generic filters, impasto mixed with matte gouache, and excess parallax. style-103 (single gouache poster layout with one loop focal point): gouache only; palette tokens unchanged; avoid busy loops, glossy effects, and fake brush jitter. Painting alone suits single painted scenes.
summary.productionApproach: Responsibilities are split. The style renderer owns paint construction, masks, and texture. A motion engine such as GSAP owns trajectories and easing, with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, timing, sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. chroma.js can validate colors and contrast. Validate with npx hyperframes check, inspect with snapshot, and render. Watch the full decoded video and verify seeks, loops, and audio sync.
